  Line 4: **Question:** How hard is it to migrate a backend integration from the Loops transactional email API (`app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional`) to Resend, and what are the concrete breaking changes between the two APIs?

  Line 10: A Loops-to-Resend transactional migration is **moderate effort, mostly a payload-shape rewrite, not an auth or infra rewrite**. The auth scheme (`Authorization: Bearer`), idempotency key header (`Idempotency-Key`, 24h window), and overall rate-limit posture (10 req/sec/team default on both) are nearly identical, and Swoosh ships **official built-in adapters for both providers** (`Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` and `Swoosh.Adapters.Resend`), so the Elixir side can be a near-mechanical adapter swap. The real work is in the four places where the two providers disagree on philosophy:

  Line 12: 1. **Templates are hosted in the dashboard on Loops and require a `transactionalId` + `dataVariables` at send time**; Resend supports the same dashboard template model (`template: {id, variables}`) but its idiomatic workflow is code-owned templates — raw `html` / `text` / `react` per send — so the migrator has to decide which side of that line the project lands on, and port every Loops template either way.

  Line 13: 2. **Loops can create a marketing Audience contact as a side-effect of a transactional send** via `addToAudience: true`; Resend has no equivalent on the transactional send path — contacts are a separate `/audiences/contacts` API used only for marketing Broadcasts.

  Line 14: 3. **Webhook event names and semantics differ** (`email.delivered`/`email.hardBounced`/`email.softBounced`/`email.spamReported` in Loops; `email.sent`/`email.delivered`/`email.bounced`/`email.failed`/`email.opened`/`email.clicked`/`email.complained`/`email.delivery_delayed`/`email.scheduled`/`email.suppressed` in Resend). The 200/400/409 status codes do not map 1:1 — Loops uses `success: bool` + `message` body for non-2xx, Resend uses standard HTTP status codes with typed `error.name` codes (e.g. `validation_error`, `missing_api_key`, `restricted_api_key`).

  Line 15: 4. **Attachments are opt-in on Loops** (requires Loops support to enable on the account) and capped at ~4 MB total JSON body; on Resend they are first-class and capped at 40 MB after base64.

1: # Migration notes
2: 
3: Notes governing the active migration from SvelteKit + Supabase to Phoenix + Ecto + Oban. AGENTS.md is an index; the detail lives here.
4: 
5: ## Database
6: 
7: - **Ecto owns all schema changes.** Supabase migrations frozen. Baseline migrations model current schema in Elixir code. Before first Phoenix/Fly release migration on an existing Supabase DB, run `bridge.sql` once to seed Ecto `schema_migrations` for the Supabase-backed baseline only; leave Oban/new cutover migrations pending. The bridge is mirrored into `supabase/seed.sql` so a local `pnpm supabase:reset` auto-seeds `schema_migrations` and leaves the DB ready for `mix ecto.migrate` (which then runs only the cutover migrations: `20260512000001` Oban + `20260611224011` pg_cron removal). The standalone `scripts/bridge.sql` remains for one-shot production use via `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f scripts/bridge.sql`.
8: - **Baseline migration fixes**: The testcontainers harness (ADR 0006) was the first time the baseline Ecto migrations actually ran against a fresh DB. This surfaced and fixed several latent bugs in the initial `4e5430e1` migration set: (1) `20260512000004` used `add :id, :bigint, default: fragment("generated by default as identity")` — invalid SQL (`DEFAULT "generated..."`); replaced with raw `CREATE TABLE` using `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY`. (2) `20260512000004` relied on `add :supabase_user_id, ..., unique: true` — but Ecto silently ignores `:unique` on `add/3` (only `:default`/`:null`/`:collation` are emitted); added an explicit `create unique_index(:user_profiles, [:supabase_user_id])` (required by the FK in `20260512000008`). (3) `20260512000006` and `20260512000008` created both a `unique_index` and a plain `index` on the same column — name collision; dropped the redundant plain indexes. (4) `20260512000006` and `20260512000010` seeded rows via raw `INSERT` missing the timestamp columns (NOT NULL from `timestamps/1`); added `NOW(), NOW()`. (5) `20260512000007` & `20260512000008` (workshop tables), `20260512000006` (`settings`), and `20260512000010` (`inventory_*`) used plain `timestamps(type: :timestamptz)` producing `inserted_at`, while production Supabase uses `created_at`/`updated_at` — all fixed to `timestamps(type: :timestamptz, inserted_at: :created_at)`. (6) `20260512000001` creates empty, source-compatible `auth.users` and `auth.identities` tables only when Supabase Auth has not already provided them. This lets the complete historical migration sequence run on stock PostgreSQL; later migration M2 removes all application FKs to those compatibility tables. The unused Supabase-only `pg_jsonschema` extension was removed and `pgcrypto` supplies `gen_random_uuid()`. 10: ## Auth / RLS
11: 
12: - **Live auth boundary (ADR 0009, ADR 0010, ALE-163)**: Phoenix owns authentication through generated Principals, magic links, opaque 30-day Sessions, and Assent Discord OAuth. SvelteKit forwards the signed `_dhc_session` cookie and consumes `{principal, roles}`; production Supabase bearer/JWT compatibility is removed. `RequireSession` checks Member access and live roles on every request. M2 renamed application ownership columns to `principal_id`, repointed 17 application FKs to `principals.id`, and retained `auth.*` only as rollback dead weight. `invitations.user_id` remains unconstrained because pending Invitations precede Principal creation. Follow `docs/auth-m2-cutover-runbook.md` for backup, smoke checks, rollback, seven-day observation, provider disablement, and credential retirement.
13: - The ALE-165/ALE-164/ALE-162/ALE-166 bullets below are historical delivery notes. Where they describe transitional dual-auth behavior or pre-M2 column names, the live ALE-163 boundary above supersedes them.
14: - **ALE-165 (Phoenix magic-link foundation, in progress)**: The first Phoenix-owned authentication path is live alongside the transitional Supabase-JWT path. `principals` + `principal_tokens` tables (migration `20260719120000_create_phoenix_auth_tables.exs`) store DHC-owned login identities, magic-link tokens (`context = "login"`, 15-min, single-use, SHA-256-hashed), and opaque DB-backed session tokens (`context = "session"`, 30-day absolute, hashed). The `Dhc.Auth` context owns magic-link issue/consume, session create/revoke, and the `load_session_principal/1` access projection (joins `user_profiles`/`user_roles` by UUID equality — the post-M1 invariant `principals.id == auth.users.id == user_profiles.supabase_user_id`; ALE-163 tightens this to a real FK after the rename). `DhcWeb.Plugs.RequireSession` is the Phoenix-session counterpart of `RequireAuth`: 401 for missing/expired/inactive, 403 for missing role. `DhcWeb.Plugs.MagicLinkRateLimit` enforces 3/email/15min and 10/IP/hour with a non-enumerating 200 body, backed by the `auth_rate_limit_windows` table. Routes: `POST /api/auth/magic-link` (public, rate-limited), `POST /api/auth/magic-link/verify` (public, sets the signed `_dhc_session` cookie), `GET /api/auth/session` + `DELETE /api/auth/session` (`:authenticated_session_api`). Magic-link delivery enqueues a `Dhc.Email.Worker` job with the `"magicLink"` friendly name (resolved to a Loops transactional ID via `MAGIC_LINK_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, provisioned in `fnox.toml`). Aggregate, non-personal telemetry: `[:dhc, :auth, :magic_link, :requested|:succeeded|:failed|:inactive_principal|:rate_limited]` and `[:dhc, :auth, :session, :rejected]`. No PII or token material in logs. Existing endpoints are unchanged and still on `RequireAuth`; ALE-163 will repoint them to `RequireSession` under the cutover.

Migration `20260719181022_ale_162_drop_auth_users_fks_add_invitation_acceptance_columns.exs` drops the four `auth.users` FK constraints (`invitations.user_id`, `user_profiles.supabase_user_id`, `user_roles.user_id`, `member_profiles.id`) and the `invitations.user_id` unique index, and adds nullable `first_name`/`last_name`/`phone_number`/`date_of_birth`/`stripe_customer_id` columns to `invitations`. Discord `auth.identities.provider_id` imports as immutable `external_identities.provider_subject`; email identities are not imported and Discord profile fields remain metadata. `Dhc.AuthMigration.M1` runs all orphan, member-correspondence, normalized-email, existing-target, provider-subject, owner, and repeated-provider gates before writing; an anomaly raises only its class/count and supports no exclusion manifest. Successful reconciliation writes aggregate source/target counts. `down/0` removes only Supabase-backed imported Principals/Discord identities, preserving Principals born through the ALE-162 Invitation lifecycle. Rehearsal tests live in `test/dhc/auth/m1_rehearsal_test.exs`; operator procedure: `docs/auth-m1-rehearsal.md`.

20: ## Workshops
21: 
22: - **Workshop RBAC drift**: The original `club_activity_registrations` RLS policy granted `beginners_coordinator` full registration visibility (carried forward in the combined `20250804190122` policy), corrected to `workshop_coordinator` by `20250923100806_fix_workshops_rls.sql`. Phoenix coordinator Workshop reads (calendar, attendees/refunds) must use `workshop_coordinator`/`president`/`admin` and must NOT reproduce the old `beginners_coordinator` policy. See the `Dhc.Workshops` moduledoc.
23: - **Member Workshop API**: `GET /api/workshops` is the member-facing Workshop collection. It is authenticated-only, defaults/constrains `status` to `planned,published`, returns counts plus current-user interest/registration state, and intentionally does not expose attendee identities or `club_activity*` join shapes. `src/routes/dashboard/my-workshops/+page.svelte` consumes it through `@dhc/api-client` rather than browser Supabase PostgREST.
24: 
25: ## Inventory
26: 
27: - **Inventory Phoenix REST contract (ALE-104)**: Inventory migration uses Phoenix/OpenAPI camelCase payloads even though persistence remains snake_case (`availableAttributes`, `parentContainerId`, `outForMaintenance`, `totalPages`, etc.). Authenticated members may read Inventory resources; `quartermaster`, `president`, and `admin` may write. Preserve current behavior during migration: category/container deletes conflict while referenced, item `PATCH` accepts `categoryId` because the current service does even though the UI does not expose category changes, item deletion is exposed in the API, and item history stays on separate `/history` endpoints rather than embedded in item detail.
28: - **Inventory Phoenix implementation**: Inventory categories, containers, items, history, commands, and dashboard statistics are Phoenix-owned. Svelte consumes the generated `@dhc/api-client`; it must not query inventory tables directly. Reuse `Dhc.Inventory.JsonArray` for jsonb columns that store arrays (`available_attributes`) because Ecto's built-in `:map` rejects lists. The camelCase↔snake_case boundary lives in controllers/renderers. Raw SQL touching `auth.users` must qualify the table (`INSERT INTO auth.users`, not `prefix: "auth"` on `Repo.query`). RBAC remains split between `:authenticated_api` reads and `:inventory_admin_api` (`quartermaster`/`president`/`admin`) writes.

30: ## Queues / Oban
31: 
32: - **Queues**: pgmq → Oban. Big-bang per-queue cutover. Discord → Email → Announcements → Stripe → Bulk Invite.
33: - **Loops transactional email**: `Dhc.Email.Worker` (queue `:emails`, `max_attempts: 5`) sends through the Swoosh transport seam (ADR 0021): it builds a `%Swoosh.Email{}` with provider options (`transactional_id`, `data_variables`, `idempotency_key: "oban-" <> job.id`) and hands it to `Dhc.Email.Mailer`, whose adapter is config per environment — `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` in prod (`POST https://app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional` via the first-party adapter), `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit` (HTTP) in dev, `Swoosh.Adapters.Test` in tests. Job args carry a **friendly name** (`inviteMember`/`workshopAnnouncement`/`workshopRegistration`/`workshopRegistrationError`/`magicLink`); the worker translates it to the provider's dashboard ID via the `:loops_transactional_ids` app-env map (built in `config/runtime.exs` + `config/dev.exs` from the `INVITE_MEMBER_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_ANNOUNCEMENT_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`/`WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_ERROR_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` env vars, all provisioned in `fnox.toml`). This mirrors the edge function's env-var lookup. Only `workshopRegistration` has a real Loops ID as its fallback default (`cmnok76cq02tq0ix92oeoi1kk`); unmapped names **cancel** the job immediately (`{:cancel, {:transactional_id_not_configured, name}}` + Sentry) — it never sends the friendly name to the provider. Error classification (ADR 0021): deterministic failures cancel (`{:cancel, _}`), 429/5xx/network errors return `{:error, reason}` for Oban backoff retries; outside prod delivery failures are swallowed so a stopped Mailpit never wedges the queue. Producers: `Dhc.WorkshopAnnouncements.Worker` (fans out 1 email job per active member), `Dhc.Invitations.BulkInviteWorker` + `Dhc.Invitations.resend_invitation_emails/1` (enqueue `inviteMember` per invite).
34: - **Worker logging convention**: Every Oban worker log line carries the job context as keyword metadata (`oban_job_id`, `oban_attempt`, `oban_queue`, `oban_worker`) plus domain-specific keys (`email`, `transactional_id`, `loops_id`, `loops_status`, `workshop_id`, `announcement_type`, `created_by`, `invitation_id`, etc.). These keys are registered in three places that must stay in sync when adding new metadata: (1) `config :logger, :default_formatter, metadata: [...]` in `config/config.exs` (local logs), (2) `config :sentry, logs: [metadata: [...]]` in `config/config.exs` + `config/runtime.exs` (Sentry Logs), (3) `Sentry.LoggerHandler` `metadata: [...]` in `config/runtime.exs` (Sentry error events from Logger). `Sentry.capture_message/2` in this Sentry version (13.1.0) does **not** accept `:contexts` — pass Oban context via `:extra` as a flat map. To avoid Sentry PII redaction (`reason: [Filtered]`) on error tuples that contain emails, pass reasons through a `reason_to_map/1` helper that stringifies keys/values rather than `inspect/1`.
35: 
36: ## API design / clients
37: 
38: - **API design**: Spec-first with OpenAPI. Custom Mix task generates Phoenix controller stubs. TypeScript client generated from spec.
39: - **PostgREST read migration**: Replace SvelteKit `supabase.from(...).select(...)` reads with domain-shaped Phoenix APIs, not table/view proxies. Track remaining call sites in [postgrest-read-migration.md](postgrest-read-migration.md); first slice is Waitlist per ADR 0005.
40: - **`.remote.ts` files**: The swap point. Rewrite from `executeWithRLS()` to `fetch(apiClient)` per domain.
41: 
42: ## Capability migration plan
43: 
44: - **Svelte service → Phoenix capability migration**: Use `src/lib/server/services/` as the behavioral inventory, but do not port service classes 1:1. Migrate for capability parity and reshape boundaries in Phoenix around domain language. Current agreed low→high complexity and recommended delivery order: Settings → Inventory → Waitlist / Onboarding Intake → Members / Membership → Invitations / Onboarding Conversion → Workshops. Track implementation complexity separately from operational risk. Stored procedures are absorbed into the owning capability (for example `insert_waitlist_entry` into Onboarding Intake and `complete_member_registration` into Invitation Acceptance), not migrated as a standalone DB-function cleanup track. Workshop migration should use vertical slices for internal/API testing, but remain Svelte-owned until full capability parity is ready to switch over.
45: - **Supabase Edge Functions are retired**: Do not add `supabase/functions` or call `supabase.functions.invoke(...)`. Bulk invitations use `POST /api/invitations`; email, Discord, announcements, and Stripe synchronization run in Oban; Stripe webhooks enter through Phoenix at `POST /api/webhooks/stripe`.
46: - **GitHub deployment workflows**: `.github/workflows/deploy-master.yml` no longer deploys Supabase Edge Functions. Do not reintroduce `supabase functions deploy`; edge-function replacements live in Phoenix/Oban. The remaining Supabase CLI job is only for `supabase/migrations/**` changes.
47:

Update the prod adapter string to `Swoosh.Adapters.Resend`; the linked `loops-to-resend-email-migration.md` is migration history, but its link should probably be reframed (or removed from this row) once the swap is complete. **Line 14** (inside the "ALE-165 (Phoenix magic-link foundation, in progress)" bullet):
> "Magic-link delivery enqueues a `Dhc.Email.Worker` job with the `"magicLink"` friendly name (resolved to a Loops transactional ID via `MAGIC_LINK_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, provisioned in `fnox.toml`)."

The bullet says "in progress" and references the runtime var `MAGIC_LINK_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` and the `fnox.toml` entry. Per ALE-262 invariants, the friendly-name → provider-ID map and all `*_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` env vars are retired; the email is sent by kebab-case alias of the Email Kind. Note: line 13 says these ALE-165/164/162/166 bullets are "historical delivery notes" superseded by ALE-163, so this could either be re-pointed or folded into the historical bucket — flag for editorial decision.

**Line 33** (heading: "Loops transactional email") — the highest-priority hit. The entire paragraph describes the Loops runtime:
- Names `Swoosh.Adapters.Loops` as the prod adapter with the `POST https://app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional` URL.
- Names the app-env map `:loops_transactional_ids` and the env vars `INVITE_MEMBER_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, `WORKSHOP_ANNOUNCEMENT_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, `WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, `WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_ERROR_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, `MAGIC_LINK_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` (implicit) — all five of which ALE-262 removes.

- Names the cancel reason `{:cancel, {:transactional_id_not_configured, name}}` — this reason tuple is a Loops-shaped sentinel; under Resend the worker no longer cancels on missing template (templates are addressable by alias directly).

> "…domain-specific keys (`email`, `transactional_id`, `loops_id`, `loops_status`, `workshop_id`, …)"
